correctness.rationale: The normalized Floquet profile is analytic at short periods because its averaged Perron eigenvalue is simple; coefficient matching forces the entire linear term to zero. Periodic integration by parts and the two Perron-weighted zero-sum identities give exactly the claimed nonnegative directed-edge quadratic energy; graph irreducibility and the common-scalar forcing factorization prove the strict and equality cases. A separate executable passes 36 exact/symbolic/numerical checks, including the exact three-season coefficient 1/18 and a four-season directed model; numerical evidence is not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: Provides the first nonzero quantitative response coefficient for rapid seasonal ecology when first-order corrections are rigorously known to vanish, valid for arbitrary number of seasons and strongly connected directed migration. The positive edge-disagreement structure and exact zero-effect classification explain how patchwise temporal mismatch changes population growth, and establish local short-period monotonicity even though prior directed examples defeat global monotonicity. The natural invariant is the local Floquet sensitivity, not an arbitrary finite or parametrically tuned numerical instance.
